sources.title: Batch 0060 frozen JVM memory-area repository context
JVMS 26 runtime data areas primary-source research packet

claims.text: The candidate divides the requested areas by sharing scope: heap and method area are JVM-wide shared areas, while each thread has its own JVM stack and pc register; per-thread areas follow thread lifetime.

The answer states that a JVM stack is per-thread and contains method frames, and that frames contain local variables, operand stack and linking/return support; it keeps references in local variables distinct from the heap allocation of class instances and arrays.

The candidate describes heap as the shared specification-level allocation area for class instances and arrays, managed by automatic storage management, without asserting a mandated collector, contiguous layout, production size or physical placement.

The answer treats the method area as a shared JVMS abstraction for per-class structures including the run-time constant pool, field/method data and code; it explicitly avoids universally equating the method area with HotSpot Metaspace or historical PermGen and preserves the specification's logical-part-of-heap wording without inferring physical co-location.

The candidate states that each thread has its own pc register, that a non-native current method has a JVM instruction address while a native current method leaves the pc value undefined, and it keeps StackOverflowError versus memory-allocation OutOfMemoryError boundaries explicit for the relevant areas.
